engagement_title: Maison Serault mark recovery for foil and engraving: recover the house wordmark and monogram from three disagreeing captures, refine them into artwork the ribbon and the engraver can actually hold, hand back the packaging application sheet editable, and run the enclosure cards for the whole collection one per piece off the card printer's own file
vertical: Fine jewelry and luxury goods: an independent European house selling pieces from 600 to 4,000 dollars through its own boutique and a small number of stockists, remaking its packaging with a new box supplier
real_brief_anchor: Ledger anchor for VECTOR-13 (Freelancer.com). The grounding note records a real posted logo production brief whose client wanted a mark that "feels unmistakably modern... bright, energetic colours paired with clean, abstract shapes", that looks "just as sharp on a website header as it does on packaging", delivered as "full-colour and single-colour versions, vector source files (AI or SVG), and high-resolution exports, along with a simple production note." The note states the brief was IP laundered to a fictional brand throughout, with no real person, brand, organisation or trademark appearing anywhere, and that it was reshaped to the connector's real capabilities. The house here is Maison Serault, the owner is Camille Roussel, and nothing real is referenced. The STRENGTHEN verdict keeps the concept and the collateral set exactly: a recovered wordmark master, a recovered monogram master, single path foil and engrave outlines of each, a reversed variant for dark stock, a packaging application sheet as an editable document, and a foil on dark presentation. What the rebuild adds is depth rather than scope. The posted brief's two hard sentences, sharp on a header and on packaging, and a simple production note, are precisely where this commission is difficult, because the packaging is a 10mm ribbon and a foil block on dark stock, and the production note is a professional statement of where the client's own mark does not hold.
client_one_liner: Our wordmark survives as one flat export and two photographs taken years apart under different light, they disagree about our own colour, and the new box supplier will not quote until someone hands them proper artwork.
client_brief:
Maison Serault is my house. I make and sell fine jewelry from one boutique and through a handful of stockists, and everything goes out in packaging that people keep.

We are changing box suppliers and they have asked for artwork. What I have is embarrassing. There is one flat export the designer who set us up sent in 2019 and never sent the working files for. There is a photograph of our wordmark on the boutique wall, which is brushed brass letters on plaster, taken with a phone under our shop lighting. And there is a photograph of one of our old cards with the monogram foil blocked on it, taken by my sister in daylight by a window.

Put the three together and they disagree about our own colour. I have stared at them for a week and I genuinely do not know which one is right. I need someone to tell me what our colour actually is and to be able to say why, because whatever you decide goes onto everything for the next ten years.

Then the artwork itself. The box supplier foil blocks. The ribbon is 10mm wide and the wordmark goes along it. The engraver does the clasp plates and needs a different kind of file again, he says, a single outline rather than a picture. And the box is a very dark stock, so the mark reverses out of it, which is the part I am most nervous about because a thin mark on dark card is exactly where things go wrong.

I would also like the application sheet, showing the mark on the box face, on the ribbon and on the card at the sizes they are really used at, plus something I can show the supplier of how the foil sits on the dark stock. That sheet has to be a file I can edit, because we will change the card copy at least twice.

There is also the card that goes in the box. Every piece leaves with a small enclosure card that names it, its reference, the metal and the stone, the price and our care line, with the monogram at the top and a little photograph of the piece. My old card printer has run these for years off one file he set by hand, and now the whole collection is being reprinted at once, so I need the run made properly from our current list rather than typed out card by card. The list is a mess, if I am honest. Two pieces share a name across two metals, one piece I have taken out of the collection is still on it, and a few pieces were never photographed.

What I need back: the wordmark and the monogram as proper artwork, the outline versions the engraver asked for, the reversed version for the box, the application sheet with whatever it was built from, the enclosure cards run for the current collection one per piece, a board I can send my supplier, and the production note. Please be honest in that note. If our mark cannot hold on the ribbon I would rather you told me now than let me find out on ten thousand metres of it.
price_band_and_audience: Fine jewelry, pieces from 600 to 4,000 dollars, buyers roughly 30 to 55 buying as a gift or for themselves, plus a small number of stockists. The band is load-bearing on the mark itself and on every canvas it appears on. At this tier the refinement is hairline and high contrast, the mark sits in a great deal of negative space, and the packaging is quiet: a small foil block on a large dark field is the whole design. A mass market jewelry house would want the opposite, a bolder mark with thicker strokes and more of it, and shipping that here would look like a different, cheaper business even if every file were technically correct. The same discipline runs through the application sheet, which is a supplier document and should read as a specification rather than as marketing, and through the presentation canvas, where restraint is the point. There is a second, harder consequence of the band: hairline refinement is exactly what a 10mm ribbon and a foil block cannot always hold, so the band creates the commission's central tension rather than merely decorating it. The ledger records the base concept at 700 to 1,500 dollars; this fuller commission, with the supplier artwork and the editable sheet, runs 1,600 to 3,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Independent European fine jewelry house making and selling pieces through its own boutique and a small number of stockists.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: An independent European house run by its founder, selling from one boutique plus a handful of stockists.
brand_identity.about: Maison Serault is a small fine jewelry house built around its founder's own hand. Pieces are made and sold through the boutique and a few trusted stockists, and everything leaves in packaging people keep. The house is changing box suppliers, and the new supplier needs proper artwork before it will quote.
brand_identity.audience: Buyers roughly 30 to 55 purchasing as a gift or for themselves, plus a small number of stockists. They value discretion and craft over logos.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Fine jewelry from 600 to 4,000 dollars. Positioned as an independent house: hairline refinement, high contrast, a small mark on a large quiet field, never mass market and never loud.
brand_identity.typography: A high contrast serif with genuine heritage credibility carries the house name. A quiet companion sets care copy and the address block. Type must never compete with the hairline foil mark.
brand_identity.voice: Spare, assured, unhurried. A line the house would write: "Each piece is finished by hand and meant to outlive its first wearer."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The working files are gone. The wordmark survives only as one flat export from 2019 whose source files were never sent, a phone photograph of brushed brass letters on the boutique wall, and a daylight photograph of the monogram foil blocked on an old card. The three disagree about the house colour, and there is no vector master of either mark.
brand_identity.values: Discretion and permanence. A decision made about the mark now sits on packaging for the next ten years, so it has to be right.

assets_supplied.name: serault_wordmark_export_2019.png
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The flat export the designer sent in 2019. It is the only file version of the wordmark that exists and he never sent the working files." A 2,600px PNG of the wordmark on a pale ground, with a warm cast over the whole image.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Its lightest brand tone sits flat at the top of the file's range, so the obvious attempt to bring that tone back returns an image in which nothing at all moves, reported as success, and a flat lightest tone is exactly what a correct flat vector export is supposed to look like. The edges in this file are nonetheless the cleanest of the three captures, so the truest colour and the best geometry are not in the same place.

assets_supplied.name: serault_wall_sign.jpg
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our wordmark on the boutique wall, brushed brass letters on plaster, taken on a phone under our shop lighting." A 4,200px frame, shot slightly from below.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Under this lighting each brass letter sits at close to the same value as its own cast shadow on the plaster, so a selection returns letter and shadow as one shape and a trace made from it thickens every stroke by a consistent amount, which reads perfectly well as the wordmark until it is set beside the export. Nothing in the selection or the trace reports that the shape includes a shadow.

assets_supplied.name: serault_card_monogram.jpg
assets_supplied.visible_description: "One of our old cards, with the monogram foil blocked on it, photographed by my sister in daylight by a window." A 3,900px frame of a cream card on a linen cloth.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Foil is a mirror, so the monogram's colour in this photograph is whatever the foil reflected from the room rather than any house colour, while the card ground carries the truest neutral of the three captures. The interlocked letterforms share enclosed counters that any route treating the monogram as one object fills in, returning a solid shape that reports success.

assets_supplied.name: serault_supplier_specs.txt
assets_supplied.visible_description: The box supplier's and the engraver's stated requirements in their own words: foil spread allowance, minimum stroke for foil on the dark stock, ribbon width at 10mm and the wordmark's used width along it, the engraver's single closed outline requirement and his minimum cut width, the box face and card dimensions, and the clear space the supplier wants around the mark.

assets_supplied.name: serault_copy.txt
assets_supplied.visible_description: The house line, the care copy that goes on the card, the boutique address block and the two pieces of packaging copy the owner expects to revise.

assets_supplied.name: serault_enclosure_card_press.pdf
assets_supplied.visible_description: The card printer's existing flat press file for the enclosure card that goes in the box with each piece: the monogram foil blocked at the head, then the piece name, a reference and metal line, a price and the house care line, with a small square window for a photograph of the piece. "The card our old printer already runs. This is his file, set by hand for one piece."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three things the printed card does not show. The piece name, the reference and metal line and the price read as three separate blocks but are set as one continuous text story in a single frame, so a field is reached by its position in that story rather than as its own object, while the care line is a second short story of its own. The monogram at the head is the printer's own crude redrawn tracing held as a group of vector paths, not a picture frame and not the recovered master, so it must be replaced rather than reused; the one genuine picture frame on the card is the small piece window, and naming the monogram as the place to bind a picture binds nothing. And the sample carries a piece name, an old reference and a price baked into its own text from the card it was set for, none of which match the current list, so the template's own words have to be replaced rather than trusted. The media box equals the trim with no bleed box present, so nothing derived from it can be delivered press ready with bleed.

assets_supplied.name: serault_collection.csv
assets_supplied.visible_description: The house's current collection as a list, one row per piece in the order the run is to print: piece name, reference, metal, stone, price, the care variant that belongs on that metal, whether the piece is still offered, and the picture cell naming the piece's own photograph.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The list is not a clean run of cards. Two pieces share a name across two metals, so a file named per piece by name collides and silently overwrites, and the key has to carry the reference. One piece is marked archived and should get no card, so the row count is not the card count. Several picture cells are simply blank because those pieces were never photographed, which no header reveals and the merge will not complain about, and pieces offered in two metals reuse one photograph across both rows. Prices are written inconsistently across rows, some with a currency mark and a thousands comma, some as a bare number, some with cents and some without.

acceptance_bar: One house colour is stated for the whole commission, with a written reason naming which capture it was taken from and why the other two were not trusted.
The wordmark and the monogram are recovered as the house's own letterforms, with no stroke thickened, thinned or reshaped by the capture it came from.
Every delivered vector carries a viewBox and no full canvas opaque background path, so it places on any ground without a box behind it.
The foil and engrave outlines are each a single closed path with every counter present as a hole rather than as a filled shape.
Both marks hold at their true delivered sizes, judged there: the wordmark at its used width on a 10mm ribbon, the monogram at card size, and both reversed on the box's dark stock.
The reversed variant is built for the dark stock and the supplier's stated foil spread rather than being the positive mark inverted.
Every supplier and engraver minimum in the supplied file is met as stated, including minimum stroke for foil, minimum cut width and clear space.
If either mark will not hold somewhere the client asked for it, that is named in writing with what to use instead, not quietly shipped at a size it cannot survive.
No invented pixels anywhere. No delivered file is larger than its source and the note lists every file any tool resized, and by how much.
The application sheet shows the mark on the box face, the ribbon and the card at the sizes they are really used at, at true physical dimensions rather than approximations.
The application sheet and the presentation canvas sit in ONE editable file, each keeping its own canvas size, delivered with the self contained source it was built from.
The words in that file are live text the client can retype and the marks in it are real vector artwork rather than pictures of a layout.
Every element the sheet depends on actually arrived in the delivered document, including anything used to show foil on dark, verified rather than assumed.
One type system across both canvases, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the weight actually used.
The whole set reads as a house selling pieces at this price rather than as a mass market jewelry brand.

The enclosure card run is one press file whose page count equals the reconciled piece count in the list's own order, plus a named file per piece, with the archived piece left out and no card carrying another piece's reference or price.
Per piece files are identifiable where two pieces share a name, and the pieces whose picture cell is blank are handled deliberately rather than left as a hole on the card.
The recovered monogram, not the card printer's decoy tracing, is what appears on the enclosure card, and it still holds at the card's used size with its counters open.

Nothing derived from the supplied card press file is claimed press ready with bleed that the file cannot carry, the shortfall is reported, and the enclosure card proofs are at press resolution at trim rather than a screen scale page enlarged to look like one.
The board carries the finished set with nothing silently missing from it.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle what lands where: the colour and both marks on imaging, the sheet and the presentation on HTML authoring, and the enclosure card run on the merge surface.
trajectory.judgement: The enclosure card run is the one genuine record per page job and lands on the merge surface, while the application sheet and the presentation are authored layout defined by a physical size and a ground and one document is defined by being editable next month. Each deliverable is placed on the surface its nature requires rather than padded onto an extra one.
trajectory.produces: A plan naming deliverable to surface and the confirmed tier.

trajectory.action: Upload the three captures and the supplier files, holding a manifest with source dimensions.
trajectory.judgement: Source dimensions are recorded here because every no invented pixels claim later is made against them.
trajectory.produces: A manifest with source dimensions per file.

trajectory.action: Preview the three captures together and triage: which capture holds each mark best as geometry, which holds the truest neutral, and what each one's light is doing to the letterforms.
trajectory.judgement: The client's assumption is that the file version is the master. Cleanest edges and truest colour are separate questions and there is no reason they resolve to the same capture, so the triage has to answer them separately before either is used.
trajectory.produces: A per capture triage note separating geometry from colour.

trajectory.action: Straighten where needed and correct each capture toward one neutral, one call per capture, recording parameters.
trajectory.judgement: Three lights need three different corrections to arrive at the same place, and a batched call applies one identical set. Averaging the casts is not recovery, it is a fourth wrong colour.
trajectory.produces: Three corrected captures with a per capture parameter log.

trajectory.action: Work the lightest brand tone in each capture toward the same place: a recovery pass on the export where its lightest area sits highest, and matching passes on the two photographs, then compare the three side by side.
trajectory.judgement: Agreeing a tone means deciding which file is allowed to be the reference rather than splitting the difference, and that decision is the one the client explicitly asked to have justified.
trajectory.produces: Three captures at one neutral and a stated view on which carries the house colour.

trajectory.action: Extract the wordmark: a selection worded at what actually distinguishes the letterforms in the chosen capture rather than at the surface they sit on, inverted for polarity, cropped to the selection bounds.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the substrate pulls the selection to the substrate, and on a brushed metal letterform the property that distinguishes it from its ground is not the obvious one.
trajectory.produces: A clean wordmark plate at source scale.

trajectory.action: Extract the monogram from the card, treating the interlocked letterforms as a graphic rather than as an object.
trajectory.judgement: Background removal is the wrong instrument on interlocked letterforms with enclosed counters and returns a solid shape that reports success, so the route has to be a selection with the correct polarity.
trajectory.produces: A monogram plate with its counters open.

trajectory.action: Trace both plates, inject a viewBox, strip the opaque full canvas path, and refine until the counters are genuine holes and each mark reduces to a single closed outline for the engraver.
trajectory.judgement: Polarity decides whether the trace is a mark or a filled box, the ground path rides along into every placement if it is not removed, and the engraver's single closed outline is a different artefact from the filled mark rather than the same file renamed.
trajectory.produces: Wordmark and monogram masters plus single path outlines.

trajectory.action: Build the reversed variant for the dark stock, allowing for the foil spread the supplier states.
trajectory.judgement: A reversed mark is not the positive inverted. Foil spreads into the stock, so the reversed artwork has to be drawn for that behaviour or the counters close on press.
trajectory.produces: Reversed artwork for both marks.

trajectory.action: Place both marks at their true delivered sizes on their true grounds and look at each: the wordmark at its used width along a 10mm ribbon, the monogram at card size, and both reversed on the dark stock.
trajectory.judgement: This is the only place the refinement can be judged, because both marks are convincing at canvas size on white, which is the only way anyone would look at them by default. Deciding to look at real size on the real ground is the agent's own move.
trajectory.produces: A verdict on both marks at their two hardest placements.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, read the family style inventories for real numeric weights, launder every name, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own and has to sit at this band without competing with a hairline foil mark. Weight cannot be inferred from a style name, a display cut is reached by its own family slug, and one bad name kills the whole kit.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry or designer and real weight per role.

trajectory.action: Search Stock with short generic queries for a dark stock or packaging ground, filter to photography, exclude generative results, license and download at full resolution, then bring it toward the recovered house neutral and lay it beside the marks.
trajectory.judgement: Choosing a ground whose light can be brought to the house neutral rather than the best thumbnail, and then judging whether the foil reads against it or disappears into it. A 240 pixel thumbnail is not evidence about a dark ground.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera scale ground, corrected and judged against the recovered colour.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML with two roots at two canvas sizes: the packaging application sheet at true physical dimensions showing box face, ribbon and card at their real used sizes with the supplier's stated clear space, and the foil on dark presentation canvas. Place both marks as inline vector inside explicitly sized and top left anchored wrappers, embed the licensed photograph as image data, and declare family and weight on every text element.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a reference is not a photograph here, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, weight is not inherited from markup semantics, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how much air the sheet carries and how quietly the mark sits.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying both canvases, retained as a deliverable in its own right.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first canvas, and parse the returned per canvas markup for the second, asserting element by element that everything the design depends on is actually present, that both marks arrived as vector shapes, that the photograph resolved to real image data, and that nothing resolves past its declared canvas width.
trajectory.judgement: Treating a successful export as unverified, and checking presence element by element rather than confirming the canvas looks broadly right. Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document with both canvases, one inspected visually and one audited in markup.

trajectory.action: Cut the enclosure card pictures from the graded piece photographs to the card window's proportion, bringing each to the same recovered house neutral the marks were settled against, and reconcile them against the collection list including the pieces whose picture cell is blank and the piece marked archived.
trajectory.judgement: The card run binds a picture per row, so the pictures are graded and cut here before the run rather than found missing on the printed sheet. A blank picture cell is not an error the merge will raise, so what a card for an unphotographed piece looks like is a decision made now, and a photograph brought to a different neutral than the marks reads as a second colour on the one card that carries both.
trajectory.produces: Card window pictures per photographed piece at the card's proportion and neutral, and a stated treatment for the pieces with none.

trajectory.surface: InDesign layout and variable data merge
trajectory.action: Convert the card printer's enclosure card press file into a working document and export its interchange form, then read what the conversion actually exposes: how many text stories and of what, which element is the real picture window and which is the decoy monogram tracing, and reconstruct the true story text so field offsets are computed from it rather than from the mapping readout.
trajectory.judgement: What the printed card looks like says nothing about how it was set, the monogram that reads like a logo well is a path group with no picture frame behind it, and the name, reference, metal and price are one flowing story whose fields are reached by position. This is also where the bleed question is answered honestly against the media box.
trajectory.produces: A working template plus a frame inventory, the reconstructed story text, and a mapping strategy chosen from what exists.

trajectory.surface: InDesign layout and variable data merge
trajectory.action: Reconcile the collection list, dropping the archived piece and settling the key that keeps two pieces sharing a name from colliding, replace the printer's baked piece name, reference and price and its decoy monogram tracing with live fields and the recovered monogram, generate and validate the mapping, prepare the template, then re-export the interchange form and confirm every expected placeholder is present.
trajectory.judgement: The client believes the list is the run. An archived piece merged produces a card for something no longer sold and a shared name overwrites a file, so both are decisions made and disclosed. Validation returns valid on offsets computed from a shortened string and preparation reports success either way, so the only evidence a field landed is finding it in the re-exported document.
trajectory.produces: A reconciled run list and a merge template whose placeholders are confirmed by inspection rather than by a success message.

trajectory.surface: InDesign layout and variable data merge
trajectory.action: Merge the reconciled list into the template binding each piece's own graded picture, render the printer's run and per piece proofs at press resolution at trim, and read what each delivered proof actually contains against its own row.
trajectory.judgement: One picture repeated across every card is what a naive run ships, resolution asked for at merge time is silently ignored so real resolution comes only from the render, and a file's position in a returned list is not evidence of which piece is inside it, so identity comes from an ordered document or a per record loop and never from output order.
trajectory.produces: The enclosure card run plus per piece proofs, each verified against its row, at press resolution at trim.

trajectory.action: Create the board and add the finished set for the box supplier, treating a partial success as partial.
trajectory.judgement: The supplier is the audience here rather than the client, so what goes on the board is what a box maker needs to quote from.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped.

trajectory.action: Write the production note: the house colour and which capture it came from and why, the correction applied per capture, minimum sizes and clear space per application, what the marks do and do not hold at ribbon width and reversed on the dark stock with what to use instead where they do not, the difference between the foil artwork and the engrave outline, the enclosure card run and every change made to the collection list to produce it, the type system, and every resize any tool reported.
trajectory.judgement: The client asked to be told now rather than after ten thousand metres of ribbon. The note has to say plainly what her own mark cannot do, which is the part of this job she cannot get anywhere else.
trajectory.produces: The written production note the supplier and the engraver both work from.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which capture is actually allowed to be the colour authority. The 2019 export is the obvious candidate because its edges are by far the cleanest and because it is the only file version of the mark, and the natural move is to correct its cast and take the house colour from it. What only running the recovery reveals is that on this file the attempt does nothing at all: the lightest brand tone already sits flat at the top of the file's range, the returned image is indistinguishable from the input, and the operation reports success with no readout of any kind that says the tone did not move. A flat lightest tone is also exactly what a correct flat vector export ought to look like, so nothing about viewing the file suggests anything is wrong. The consequence is structural rather than cosmetic: the truest colour has to come from one of the photographs, which are the softer sources, while the cleanest geometry stays in the export, so colour and geometry are separated across two files and the client's stated assumption about her own master file is wrong.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and care cannot pre empt it. Whether a tone can be recovered is a property of the file's own range, there is no measurement available anywhere in the connector, and the only signal is the visible difference between input and output, which is nil. An agent that corrects the cast carefully and reads the result at normal viewing size sees a file that looks entirely reasonable. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the three captures disagree about the house colour and asks to be told which is right and why, which is a client describing her problem and asking for the judgement she is paying for. No asset note, deliverable or earlier step says the export is unrecoverable or that the answer lies in a photograph. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is to change which file is the authority for colour, re correct the other two toward it instead of toward the export, and then carry a colour from one capture onto a mark whose geometry comes from another, which is a different method rather than the same operation on changed input.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re establish the neutral from the capture that actually holds it, re correct the other two toward that reference rather than toward the export, and re examine the wordmark plate, since it was extracted from a file that is now the geometry source only and its colour cannot be trusted for any downstream spec. Then write the reason down, because the client asked for the justification as an explicit deliverable and the reason is now specific rather than general.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The house adopts a wrong colour, taken from the one capture that could not be corrected, and it goes onto boxes, ribbon, cards and clasp plates for a decade because everything in the recovery reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the refined mark survives the ribbon and the dark stock. Both marks are entirely convincing at canvas size on white. At the wordmark's used width along a 10mm ribbon the high contrast letterforms lose their hairlines, and reversed on the box's dark stock with the supplier's stated foil spread the counters in the monogram's interlocked letterforms close into solid, so what the client would receive is a foil block with an unreadable smudge in the middle of it and a ribbon carrying a broken line of type. Both artefacts pass every structural check: single closed path, counters present as holes, viewBox correct, minimum stroke met as drawn. The failure is what the physical process does to a drawing that is correct on screen, and nothing in any response measures or reports it. The tracing step takes no options, so the only levers are the raster preparation and the drawing itself, and which lever is needed cannot be chosen until the failure has been seen at real size on the real ground.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it. The marks have to exist before they can be placed, no measurement is available, and meeting a stated minimum stroke as drawn does not establish that the mark reads once foil spreads into dark stock at that size. An agent that refines carefully and respects every stated minimum still gets closed counters, because the variable is the house's own high contrast letterforms at 7mm, not the care taken. (b) Nothing states it. The supplier file gives the ribbon width, the used width, the foil spread allowance and the minimum stroke, which is the constraint, and the brief says a thin mark on dark card is where things go wrong, which is the client naming her worry exactly as she would to a designer. Neither says which counter closes, on which mark, or at which of the two placements. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is a drawing decision: open the counters and weight the hairlines for a ribbon cut that is a genuinely different artefact from the master, or accept that the refined mark is a large format asset and build a separate small size lockup, either of which changes the application sheet's composition and the production note.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to the raster preparation and to the drawing to produce a ribbon cut with opened counters and a heavier hairline rather than trying to rescue the master by scaling it, re trace, re strip the ground path and inject the viewBox again, then re place at ribbon width and reversed on the dark stock rather than assuming the heavier version took. Check the placement that was not flagged at the same real size. If neither mark holds at ribbon width, state what carries the ribbon instead and re author the application sheet around the mark's real minimum size, which is a different sheet.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A house that sells pieces at four figures wraps them in ribbon carrying a broken wordmark and boxes carrying a foil block with a closed up monogram in it, having been handed artwork that was flawless in every file she was shown, and finds out after the supplier has run the order.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the delivered document actually contains. The application sheet's entire job is to show a hairline foil mark reversing out of a dark ground at real size, and the constructs that express foil, sheen, a debossed edge, a hairline rule around a reversed panel, are exactly the ones whose treatment on import cannot be predicted: some survive intact, some are silently dropped so the element renders as a flat shape, and at least one route makes a text element present in the document and completely invisible on the canvas. The export returns success identically in every case, with no warning of any kind, and the visual preview resolves the first canvas only, so the second canvas exists solely as returned markup. An element that vanished and an element that arrived look the same from the response. The available documentation is not a substitute for looking either, since it is wrong in both directions on several constructs, claiming support that fails and warning against things that work.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it. The document has to be exported before its contents can be inspected, and no amount of care at authoring time establishes what a given construct became, because the failures are silent and the response is identical. Choosing conservative constructs everywhere is not the answer either: the sheet has to show foil on dark convincingly enough for a supplier to quote from it, and that is the whole design problem. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for an editable sheet showing the mark at real sizes and something showing how the foil sits on the dark stock. No asset, acceptance line or earlier step says which construct will be normalised or dropped. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is to re author the affected panel out of different constructs, which is a design change to the sheet rather than a re export of the same page, and it may change how the foil is represented at all.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Identify from the returned markup exactly which elements arrived and in what form, re author the affected panel with constructs that survive rather than adjusting the ones that did not, re export, and re verify per canvas rather than assuming the second attempt took. Check the canvas that was not flagged at the same element by element level, since only one of the two canvases can be seen and the other has never been established as correct.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The client sends her new box supplier an application sheet on which the foil panel is a flat rectangle and part of the specification text is present but invisible, and the supplier quotes from it.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether each delivered enclosure card proof actually carries the piece its filename claims, and whether the monogram on the card still reads at card size. The natural way to hand the client a proof per piece is a multi record raster run, and the tool's own description says one output file per row and hands back a list labelled by row number. Those labels are not to be trusted: multi record raster output comes back in an order that does not match the roster while the response still names it by row, so a proof named for one piece can contain another piece's reference and price. Every gate above it passes, the count is right and each file is a valid card. Separately, the run is the first time the monogram sits at the card's real used size beside live text and a photograph rather than alone on white, and at that size the interlocked counters that were open on the master can begin to close, which only shows on the rendered card.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it: the mislabelling is in the response itself and the response is the only thing an agent that trusts its tools would use to name the files, and the monogram's behaviour at card size is a property of the drawing meeting the size, learnable only after the card is rendered. (b) Nothing states it: the acceptance line about the right piece's own price is the house's requirement and no asset says which route mislabels or which counter closes. (c) It is not a propagation re run: the response is a different delivery route, a single ordered multi page run or a per record loop producing one file at a time so identity is guaranteed, and if the monogram closes it is a return to the raster preparation and the drawing rather than a re merge.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Abandon the multi record raster route, re run the enclosure cards through a route whose record identity is guaranteed, rename every proof from what is actually inside it, re check the two pieces that share a name so the collision does not overwrite, and if the monogram closes at card size return to the raster preparation and the drawing to open its counters at that size before the run is trusted.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A house that sells pieces at four figures encloses each one with a card carrying another piece's reference and price, or a card whose monogram has closed into a blot at the size it is actually printed, discovered by a customer opening the box rather than by the house.

deliverables.name: Maison Serault wordmark and monogram masters
deliverables.spec: Both house marks recovered as the house's own letterforms from captures that disagree, delivered as placeable, scalable vector geometry with a real viewBox and no opaque full canvas ground path, with every counter present as a genuine hole and no stroke thickened or thinned by the capture it came from. Supplied alongside the engraver's artefact, a single closed outline of each mark meeting his stated minimum cut width, and the reversed variant drawn for the box's dark stock and the supplier's stated foil spread rather than produced by inverting the positive.

deliverables.name: True colour reference set
deliverables.spec: The three captures, taken years apart under three different lights, brought to one neutral so the house colour can be stated and defended, with a per capture parameter log and a written statement of which capture the colour was taken from and why the other two were not trusted. This is the deliverable the client asked for by name when she said she needs to be told what her colour is and to hear why, and it is the reference every foil and ink specification downstream is written against.

deliverables.name: Packaging application sheet and foil on dark presentation as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: A single native editable document carrying the packaging application sheet at true physical dimensions, showing the mark on the box face, along the 10mm ribbon and on the card at the sizes they are really used at with the supplier's stated clear space, plus a foil on dark presentation canvas, each root keeping its own canvas size. Live editable text in one licensed type system, both marks as real vector shapes, the licensed ground carried as embedded image data, delivered with the self contained source it was authored from because the card copy changes at least twice.

deliverables.name: Enclosure card run for the collection
deliverables.spec: The card printer's single enclosure card press file reverse engineered into a live merge template, the printer's decoy monogram tracing replaced by the recovered monogram and the name, reference, metal and price reached as live fields by position in the one story they share, then run against the reconciled collection list: one press file whose page count equals the reconciled piece count in the list's own order, plus per piece named files whose identity is guaranteed rather than inferred from output position and whose key survives two pieces sharing a name, each piece's own graded photograph bound through the card's single real picture window, the pieces with no photograph handled deliberately and the archived piece left out, with proofs at press resolution at trim and the bleed reality of the supplied file reported.

deliverables.name: Production note and supplier board
deliverables.spec: A written production note the box supplier and the engraver both work from: the house colour and its justification, the correction applied per capture, minimum size and clear space per application, the difference between the foil artwork and the engrave outline, an honest statement of what each mark does and does not hold at ribbon width and reversed on the dark stock with what to use instead where it does not, the type system by role with foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight, and every resize any tool reported. Paired with a persistent shareable board carrying the finished set for the supplier.

decision_gates: Which capture is allowed to be the authority for colour and which for geometry, and what to do when they are not the same file.
Whether a tone that will not move is a correct flat colour or an unrecoverable one, and how to tell the client the difference.
How far each of three lights is pushed to reach one neutral, and where correcting a capture becomes inventing a colour.
How to word a selection on brushed metal letterforms whose value sits close to their own cast shadow.
Whether the monogram is treated as an object or as a graphic, given interlocked letterforms with shared enclosed counters.
How much refinement the letterforms take, since hairline refinement is what the price band wants and what the ribbon cannot always hold.
Whether the reversed variant is drawn for foil spread or produced by inverting the positive.
Whether a mark that fails at ribbon width is opened up into a separate small size cut or declared a large format asset, and what carries the ribbon if it is.
How the sheet represents foil on dark at all, given that the most convincing constructions are the least predictable ones.
Whether to verify the delivered document element by element or accept that a successful export is a correct one.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a hairline foil mark it must not compete with.
What to escalate in writing versus what to fix silently, on a commission where the client explicitly asked to be told now rather than after the ribbon is run.
Which deliverables are authored panels the client edits herself and which is a genuine record per page run at volume, given the enclosure card run is one card per piece off the printer's own file.

How to reconcile a collection list the client believes is the run, given an archived piece that should get no card, two pieces sharing a name across two metals, and pieces with no photograph, and which key names a file so a shared name does not silently overwrite.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the three captures into a frontier image model and it draws a new jewelry logo. IDENTITY is the whole commission: this is one house's existing wordmark and monogram, surviving only as a 2019 export, a photograph of brass letters on a wall and a photograph of a foil block on a card, and a regenerated mark is simply a different house with the same name. SPEC is a manufacturing specification: a single closed outline at a stated minimum cut width for the engraver, artwork drawn for a stated foil spread on a named dark stock, a wordmark at a used width along a 10mm ribbon, clear space to the supplier's rule. A generated picture satisfies none of it, cannot be quoted from, and cannot be checked. The enclosure cards compound this: they are a record per page run bound to the house's own current list, one card per piece carrying that piece's own reference and price at press resolution at trim, which a generated image neither produces nor can be checked against, and the list has to be reconciled and its pictures cut rather than typed out. EDITABILITY is an explicit deliverable: one document with live text and real vector geometry that the owner revises when the card copy changes, not a flat image of a layout. And the core of the engagement is judgement about material reality that no render can perform: deciding which of three disagreeing captures is telling the truth about a colour that will sit on ten years of packaging, and telling a client honestly that her own mark will not survive her own ribbon. The client asked for that second thing by name, and it is advice rather than an image.
doability_proof: Five surfaces, honestly counted and deliberately not padded. image_vectorize is counted inside the Photoshop and Lightroom surface rather than as an Illustrator surface, and the Illustrator vector tools are never called because document_render_vector and document_merge_data_vector sit on a polling helper that does not exist in this host; the enclosure card run is a genuine record per page job, so it is carried on the InDesign layout merge chain, which is fully headless and synchronous in this host, rather than on that vector helper or manufactured. Every link is verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account). IMAGING: headless upload through asset_initialize_file_upload, curl PUT and asset_finalize_file_upload, then asset_inline_preview before any adjustment or crop, auto_straighten, masked and unmasked apply_adjustments, the highlight and temperature tools, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, fill_area and vectorize are all verified live and synchronous. The verified extract chain of selection worded at the mark's own visual properties, inversion for polarity, crop to the selection's bounds and trace is exactly the route both marks take, and the verified finding that naming the substrate returns the substrate is the live gate on the wall sign. remove_background is documented as returning a solid opaque shape rather than punching an enclosed interior, and as collapsing on disjoint lettering, which is why it is never the route to a counter here. image_vectorize takes no options at all, emits no viewBox and always emits an opaque first path, all verified, so every refinement the deliverable gates on is genuine work in the raster and in the SVG. There is no eyedropper, no hex readout and no ruler anywhere in the family, which is why the colour decision is scored as a stated judgement with a reason rather than as a measurement, and why the mark's survival at ribbon width is scored by eye on the real ground. crop_and_resize is documented as interpolating to a hard cap and reporting it only in the tradeoffs array, so the no invented pixels bar is a decision plus a disclosure. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt with its validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout with additionalImageFiles and document_render_layout are verified fully headless and synchronous, one record per page for PDF output with page count equal to row count, per record identity guaranteed by createSeparateFiles or a recordRange loop, and 300 dpi at trim coming from the render rather than from the merge, where a resolution asked for at merge time is silently ignored. The card template's field granularity is reverse engineered from the converted document rather than assumed: the name, reference, metal and price are reachable only by position inside one story, the decoy monogram is a group of vector paths with no picture frame behind it so the recovered monogram is placed rather than bound, the one genuine picture frame is the piece window, and no bleed can be introduced into anything derived from a media box that equals its trim. The per proof identity checkpoint rests on the verified finding that multi record PNG and JPEG output comes back reversed while the response labels it by row, with PDF, createSeparateFiles and a recordRange loop the three verified trustworthy routes; the merge binding each row's own picture through additionalImageFiles is verified, and a blank picture cell merges without complaint so it is a decision rather than an error. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, absolute mm units resolve to exact physical canvases at 96 dpi, inline SVG becomes native editable vector shapes, gradients, borders, radius, opacity and a single shadow layer survive, and the verified silent drops are real: external image URLs render as empty placeholders, a data URI in a CSS background is dropped entirely, blend modes, blurs, text shadows and outlines are dropped, multi layer shadows truncate to the first layer, and a stroked transparent text element arrives fully invisible. The importer returns success in every one of those cases with no warning, and the rendition preview resolves the first canvas only, which is why verification is split between a visual check and a markup audit. The right anchored auto sized wrapper failure is a verified live finding the trajectory designs against. Transport goes through the text/html upload path because the embedded ground photograph exceeds the inline threshold, and persistence is not assumed, so the deliverable is the editable document plus the self contained source. FONTS: the recommend, styles, find, kit chain is verified end to end in a real browser, and the non standard numeric weights, the display cut by slug rule, the slug not PostScript CSS rule and the all or nothing kit call are live findings the task leans on. STOCK AND BOARDS: short generic queries only because long queries return zero hits, the orientation filter is never passed because it is verified broken, licensing returns genuine camera scale photography with a generative flag exposed so it can be excluded, and boards persist with a twelve placement cap where 201 means partial success with a failed items list. VOLUME: seven client files in, roughly twenty image artefacts moved plus a one record per page enclosure card run at the reconciled piece count, every multi image call at or under the ten item cap and no batch above twenty. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no fill_text, no animate_design, no create_firefly_board, no replace_image, no download_design, no upscaling, no OCR, no compositing, no AI object removal, no from scratch generation, and no photograph reaching Express as a URL.
